modern: From Plato: The man who has a lofty mind and takes a view of all time and of all substance, do you suppose it possible for him to think that human life is anything great? It is not possible, he said.—Such a man, then, will think that death also is no evil.—Certainly not.
original: From Plato: The man who has an elevated mind and takes a view of all time and of all substance, dost thou suppose it possible for him to think that human life is anything great? It is not possible, he said.—Such a man then will think that death also is no evil.—Certainly not.
